_provenance: Owner-confirmed list of six. I originally proposed ten; the owner cut four — fat-loss, anxiety-management, emotional-regulation, hormonal-health — on the grounds that applying it there would buy my caution at the price of most of the mindset domain, and that those belong under rule 13 (signals and caveats) like everything else. Do not re-add a category here without asking: this file raises the bar and narrowing the candidate pool is the owner's decision, not a research judgement. first-aid added later, owner-confirmed, with a rationale the owner was explicit should NOT be generalised — see the entry itself.
_comment: Categories where acting on bad advice can cause physical harm, delay treatment someone needs, or worsen a crisis. The bar is higher here and an empty category is explicitly preferred to an adjacent one: a bad recommendation costs more than an absent one. Owner's ruling, made about addiction-recovery and generalised. Adding a category here raises the standard; it never lowers one.

categories.addiction-recovery: Dependence, withdrawal and relapse. Wrong or moralising advice can keep someone from treatment, and some withdrawal is medically dangerous.
categories.injury-rehab: Loading an injury wrongly causes further injury. Physical and immediate. Anything here is education, never assessment.
categories.back-pain-management: The category most likely to attract confident structural claims that frighten people out of moving, which is itself the harm.
categories.grief-and-loss: People arrive acutely bereaved. Prescriptive stage models and timelines do documented harm.
categories.supplements-literacy: DEFINITIONAL rather than precautionary, and the owner's framing is the right one: this category exists to teach someone how to JUDGE supplement claims. A creator who sells supplements is working against the category's own purpose, not merely carrying a conflict to be disclosed. This is the one place where commercial interest is disqualifying rather than a rule-13 signal, and it is disqualifying because of what the category is for.
categories.therapy-literacy: The failure mode is steering someone away from help or toward the wrong modality. Narrowing here is only moderate, so the standard is cheap to hold.
categories.first-aid: ACUTE-RECALL, and the owner was specific that this reasoning is narrower than the other six. It is not that bad advice here is costly over time. It is that the content gets recalled under acute stress by someone who has no capacity to evaluate it in the moment — no time to check a second source, no attention left to notice that the presenter is confident rather than qualified. Everywhere else the visitor retains some ability to judge what they were told; here that ability is exactly what the situation removes. Do not extend this rationale to a category merely because its subject sounds serious: the test is whether the content is acted on under stress, from memory, with evaluation impossible.

standard: Prefer a documented empty category to an adjacent or under-credentialed creator.
A creator here should normally carry the `credentialed` signal, or the record must say plainly why they are trustworthy without it.
`notFor` and `caveats` must state the limit explicitly — that this is education and not assessment or treatment.
A creator whose framing discourages professional help needs that named in their record, not softened.
In supplements-literacy only, selling the product class is disqualifying rather than disclosable — see the note on that category.
In first-aid only, the acute-recall rationale applies. It is not a general licence to raise the bar wherever harm is imaginable — see that category's entry.
